description: Employer-owned careers/ATS endpoints missing for eight of the nine banks in the cell.
Foreign-parent IR/press rooms (KBC, Erste Group, RBI, UniCredit SpA, Intesa Sanpaolo) are the true origin layer for HU-subsidiary board changes but are not clearly inside this cell.

The nine named banks are not the full HU systemic issuer set; state-owned and specialist institutions (MFB, Eximbank, Takarékbank legacy entities, Magyar Posta/ MBH-adjacent entities, Oberbank HU, Cetelem, Sberbank successor perimeter) were not covered.
Issuer-owned social channels (LinkedIn company pages, YouTube, Facebook) were not scouted, although banks announce appointments and hiring campaigns there first and in Hungarian.
No RSS/Atom/JSON feed was confirmed for any of the nine press rooms; all collection plans currently assume HTML/PDF scraping.
Historical depth of each press room (how far back the index paginates) is unknown, so no baseline period for leadership-move rates can be set.

I could not exercise the actual query mechanics of the three core event sources (MNB határozatok és végzések keresése, cegkozlony.hu/kereses, kozzetetelek.mnb.hu lekérdező) — parameter names, pagination, date filtering, rate limits and anti-bot behaviour are unknown.

No crosswalk was found between MNB institution identifiers (Intézménykereső registration numbers) and cégjegyzékszám / adószám, which is required to join regulator decisions to company-register officer events.
Savings cooperatives, small pénzügyi vállalkozások, PSD2 payment/e-money institutions and independent intermediaries are inside the statutory regime but were not individually enumerated in this pass.

EU-level registers that mirror or supplement HU officeholder/entity data (EBA credit institutions register, ESMA registers, SSM/ECB fit-and-proper for significant institutions such as OTP) were not searched in this cell.
The publication lag between an actual appointment, the MNB decision, the Cégközlöny entry and the e-cégjegyzék refresh has not been measured.

This cell's regulatory/statutory sources cover officeholders well but carry almost no signal on the 'jobs / hiring' topic (vacancy volumes, headcount trends) beyond annual headcount in e-beszámoló filings.

Reuse and redistribution rights differ sharply across sources: MNB/Cégközlöny/e-beszámoló are free public-sector information, while OCCSZ extracts and OPTEN/Céginfo data are licensed products, and all officer data is personal data under GDPR.

State-influenced (rather than state-owned) financial actors — e.g. banks with state or state-linked shareholding, Gránit/MBH-type structures, KAVOSZ/Széchenyi Kártya programme operators, Posta Biztosító — were not systematically enumerated in this pass.
Only TED has a confirmed documented API/bulk-download route. Magyar Közlöny, Hivatalos Értesítő, Cégközlöny, EKR and KÖZIGÁLLÁS have no API confirmed in this pass.
The cell's pointer role — mining procurement awards for supplier names serving state financial bodies — was identified but not exercised; no award-notice supplier extraction was performed.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature: only TED and entity English pages publish in English; gazette and company-register material is Hungarian-only.
No assessment was made of how far back each portal's archive reaches (gazette archives, Cégközlöny back-issues, TED pre-2011 bulk).

No source found covering the big global SI/outsourcing layer in Hungary (IBM, T-Systems Hungary, Accenture, DXC, Deloitte/EY technology arms), which typically staffs the largest private-bank programmes.
Domestic banking-software vendors beyond Finshape were not covered: Dorsum, Cellum, Microsec, NetLock, Scriptum, R34DY, Sysdata and similar.
Vendor-run and trade-run conference agendas (CIO Hungary, Portfolio Banking Technology / Hitelezés, IT Business events) were identified only in passing, not catalogued.
Foreign vendors (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Thales, IDEMIA, Nexi) publish nothing in Hungarian, so no local-language terms exist for their HU appointments.
No archival/indirect-reveal channel established for vendor pages that get quietly edited (customer-logo walls, leadership pages).
State-adjacent procurement visibility for bank-serving vendors was not explored, despite 4iG's state framework contracts being under review.
Past-edition speaker pages are the core value of this cell (title drift between editions), but several organisers rewrite or retire event URLs; no snapshot layer is in place.
Current-year jury and speaker rosters for Év Bankja and for TechShow X 2026 were not directly confirmed page-by-page in this pass.

Insurance-adjacent and savings-cooperative/neobank events, and vendor-hosted client days (core-banking and card-processing suppliers), were not enumerated; these carry mid-level operations and IT titles.
Hungarian job titles vary in wording across organisers for the same role, and English event pages give different renderings; no normalisation dictionary exists yet.

Only the Mastercard Év Bankja programme was mapped; other Hungarian financial awards and shortlists (marketing, IT, employer-brand, insurance awards) that also publish juries and named entrants were not covered.
Case-level collective-redundancy notifications filed via ESTAT to county/Budapest government offices are not open data.

Only the UniCredit Bank Hungary company union was clearly identified as a live, active company-level union in banking. Equivalent bodies at OTP, MBH, Erste, K&H, Raiffeisen, CIB and Gránit were not located in this pass.

The official Hungarian civil-organisation registry (birosag.hu civil szervezetek névjegyzéke) and the official company register (e-cegjegyzek / Cégközlöny) were not directly searched in this pass; only the commercial aggregator Céginfo was found.
Annual reports / e-beszámoló filings of individual Hungarian banks, which carry audited average headcount figures, were not probed; only MBH's disclosure page and bond prospectus were reached.
No source of Hungarian labour-court decisions (birosag.hu anonimizált határozatok) was assessed, although the UniCredit union-president dismissal is explicitly heading to court.

English-language coverage of Hungarian bank workforce contraction is thin and mostly routed through Eurofound ERM; no Hungarian-focused English trade outlet (e.g. BBJ, Telex English) was confirmed as a systematic source.

Only OTP, MBH, Gránit and UniCredit were reached at issuer-report level. K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, CIB, Erste/other jelzálogbank issuers, Magyar Bankholding legacy entities, MFB, Eximbank and the savings-cooperative successors have no per-bank annual-report source entry yet.

Payments-side actors (pénzforgalmi intézmények, e-money issuers, acquirers and fintechs such as OTP Mobil/Simple, Barion, Global Payments Hungary, Revolut's HU entity, Wise HU) were not individually sourced; the payment sector was covered only through the generic registers.

English-language equivalents of the archival layer (IFRS 'Annual Report' English editions, EBA/ECB-level registers, GLEIF LEI records of HU bank entities with legal-name and status change history) were not sourced.

No source was established for branch-network and site-level organisational footprint (fiókhálózat closures), which is the physical correlate of headcount reduction and a strong organization-change signal.
Two of the highest-value routes (bulk filing dataset, OPTEN officer-change history) are commercial and their terms were not read; scraping either would likely breach ToS.

Regional universities outside Budapest — Debreceni Egyetem, Szegedi Tudományegyetem, Miskolci Egyetem, Pécsi Tudományegyetem — were not individually crawled for bank partnership and traineeship announcements; only Corvinus and BME were covered.

County chambers of commerce (Hajdú-Bihar and Csongrád-Csanád Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara) and county government offices (kormányhivatal) labour-market bulletins were not explored, despite being the bodies that publish local vacancy statistics and host employer announcements.

Commercial real-estate/office-market sources (CBRE, Colliers, JLL Budapest office market reports, Debrecen office park leasing news) were not covered. Large office lettings by financial GBS tenants precede headcount ramp-ups and are publicly reported.

State-aid and subsidy decision records (individual government decrees on 'egyedi kormánydöntés' / EKD subsidies published in Magyar Közlöny) were not searched, although these are the legally mandated publication of every subsidised job-creation project including service centres.

Employer-brand and graduate-survey sources (e.g. Randstad Employer Brand Research Hungary, Universum/Most Attractive Employers rankings, Diákmunka/graduate career fairs at regional universities) were not covered; these reveal which banks are competing hardest for the graduate pool.

No Hungarian-language equivalent term was identified for 'GBS' as used locally; Hungarian coverage uses 'üzleti szolgáltató központ' / 'szolgáltató központ' / 'SSC', while 'GBS' appears almost exclusively in English-language trade press.

The cell's six seeded actors are only a fraction of HU-licensed payment and e-money institutions. Smaller PSPs, e-money issuers, PISP/AISP third-party providers and BNPL/wallet players were not enumerated in this pass.

No direct feed of statutory officer changes (Cégközlöny / e-cégjegyzék, the official company gazette and registry) was located or tested in this pass; only commercial aggregators (Nemzeti Cégtár, OPTEN) were found.

The strongest quantitative hiring signals (LinkedIn HU job counts, Glassdoor review flow) sit behind ToS that forbid automated collection, and the two most useful first-party career sites (Revolut, Wise) are JS-rendered.
Named role-holders gathered here (SimplePay, Revolut HU, PayU HU, Barion officers) are drawn from media and aggregator snapshots of varying dates and are not point-in-time verified.

Sector events (FinTechShow, Internet Hungary) surfaced only incidentally. Speaker rosters and award shortlists are a systematic census of who currently holds which role, but no event-source monitoring was set up.
Visa's Hungary/CEE country organisation has no identified first-party or trade source for appointments.
No press-release wire source was scouted (MTI Országos Sajtószolgálat / OS.hu), which is where Hungarian corporate appointment announcements are frequently distributed verbatim.
Generic job-board coverage for the rails layer (profession.hu, cvonline.hu, LinkedIn Jobs, hvg allas) was not scouted; only GIRO's own ATS was found.
Cégközlöny itself (the official company gazette) was identified conceptually via legislation and secondary explainers, but no working access URL/feed for its published change entries was confirmed.
Domestic POS/ATM service and deployment companies beyond the multinationals (e.g. bank-owned acquiring units, terminal service providers, cash-in-transit/ATM outsourcers) were not enumerated.
Few genuine 'pointer' sources were found beyond HR Portál and the Bankszövetség directory; no HU executive-search/HR newsletters or payments-community groups were identified.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live; all reachability assessments are inference from search-result metadata only. globalpay.hu was seen only as an HTTP legacy URL.

No wire-service source identified in this cell. MTI/OS (Országos Sajtószolgálat) is the upstream that many of these outlets republish verbatim; adding it would give earlier, deduplicated, structurally uniform appointment items.

Cell coverage is heavily skewed to C-suite and deputy-CEO appointments. Ordinary hiring signals (open vacancies, headcount growth, new team builds in payments/cards/IT) are not covered by the press channel at all.

Payments-specific actors (card schemes, acquirers, PSPs, ATM/POS vendors, GIRO/Takarékinfo-type infrastructure) are far less covered by these general business outlets than banks are; discovered examples were almost entirely bank-side.

Only one en-language Hungary-focused outlet (BBJ) was captured; other English channels (Hungary Today, Daily News Hungary, Telex English, Reuters/Bloomberg Hungary coverage) were not scouted in this pass.

No archival/backfill strategy established. Executive career-path history (who moved from OTP to MBH, when) requires multi-year archive access; mfor.hu and HR Portál tag pages look like the best backfill assets but pagination depth is unknown.
Robots.txt / terms-of-service posture for automated collection was not inspected for any domain in this cell.
No English-language newsroom was located in this pass for the Hungarian subsidiaries of Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, K&H/KBC and MBH Bank — only group-level or HU-language pages surfaced.

Coverage found is almost entirely about senior appointments; the 'jobs/hiring' topic (headcount, recruitment drives, layoffs, shared-service-centre staffing in Budapest) is unrepresented in this English cell.

The payments half of the sector is thinly covered in English at the Hungary level: apart from Mastercard/Visa scheme newsrooms, no English source was found covering Hungarian PSPs, acquirers or fintechs (e.g. Barion, OTP Mobil/Simple, Nexi/SIA Hungary, Diebold/Printec-type vendors).

No structured/machine-readable disclosure channel was captured for this cell beyond issuer pages: the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE/BÉT) English regulatory-announcement feed, where OTP and other listed financials file appointment disclosures, was not reached.

Several strong candidates (BBJ appointments section, FinTech Futures job-cuts vertical) were identified structurally, but the depth and stability of their archives — pagination limits, URL scheme changes such as BBJ's /whosnews/ to /business/people/appointments/ migration — were not tested.
Payments-sector actors (OTP Mobil/SimplePay, GIRO Zrt., Revolut Hungary, Wise Budapest, PayPal/Global Payments/Worldline local entities, ATM and terminal vendors) lack confirmed social handles.
No headcount-growth baseline has been captured for any Hungarian bank or PSP; the 'employee growth curve' signal named in the cell rationale requires a first snapshot to become a time series.
The Hungarian announcement-phrase lexicon is validated for only one idiom; variants ('büszkén jelentem be', 'új fejezet kezdődik', 'kinevezésemről', 'gratulálunk') are untested.
No compliant technical collection path has been identified for the auth-walled core of this cell.

Adjacent self-publication channels not examined: employer-branding subpages (LinkedIn Life tabs), Instagram/TikTok recruitment content, Hungarian professional communities (e.g. Facebook groups for banking professionals), and personal blogs/Substacks of Hungarian fintech figures.
Missing own-ATS feeds for Erste Hungary, CIB Bank, Magyar Bankholding-adjacent entities, Takarekbank legacy units, and the HU savings/credit-institution long tail.
Payments-specific employers (PSPs, acquirers, POS/ATM vendors, card processors, wallet providers) are under-covered versus banks.
Workday, SAP SuccessFactors and Oracle/Taleo tenants used by foreign-owned HU banks were not enumerated; only Nexum karrierportal.hu, Greenhouse, Lever and SmartRecruiters patterns were established.
Sources found give current-vacancy snapshots only; no historical baseline exists, so 'burst' detection has nothing to compare against.
Leadership moves are only weakly observable from vacancy data; executive-search mandates and confidential agency ads were not systematically mapped.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live; all liveness statements are search-result-derived.

PSP Siklóssy & Partner, HILL International Kft., Kienbaum Executive Consultants Kft. and ISG International Executive Consulting Kft. appear on the Hungarian executive-search revenue ranking but have no confirmed source entry in this slice.

LinkedIn is where Hungarian executive search firms actually announce mandates and completed placements ('örömmel jelentjük be', 'új vezető'), but no LinkedIn-based collection design was produced here beyond noting the Amrop company page.
Payments-specific talent intelligence (PSPs, acquirers, card schemes, fintech/PSD2 compliance roles) is absent — every source found treats 'pénzügy' as banking/accounting/insurance.

No HR-consultancy (as opposed to recruitment-agency) labour-market analysts were captured — e.g. the Big Four HR advisory practices, RSM Hungary (whose middle-manager salary analysis surfaced incidentally in Trenkwalder coverage), or academic/KSH labour analysts covering financial-services employment.

The two most complete structured datasets in this cell — the BBJ Book of Lists rankings and full recruiter salary-guide PDFs — are paywalled or lead-capture gated, and no fetch verification of any URL was performed in this pass.
Only current editions were located; historical archives of Hays HU salary guides and Manpower MEOS HU finance-sector readings were not enumerated, so no back-series exists yet.

Member rosters for IVSZ (/tagok/), MAFISZ (/hu/tagok/), Magyar Lízingszövetség and MAKISZ were identified but their full contents were not enumerated in this pass; the Bankszövetség roster was read only in summary (~67 entries, exact names not fully captured).

The mid-level committee/working-group layer (Bankszövetség munkacsoportok, IVSZ Fintech Munkacsoport, AmCham committees, JVSZ working groups) is where payments and IT decision-makers are named, but only the index pages were located, not the chair lists.

Only AmCham, BCCH and DUIHK/AHK were touched. Not examined: MKIK (Magyar Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara) and its Budapest chapter BKIK, Joint Venture Szövetség (JVSZ) own site, French/Italian/Dutch/Nordic chambers, and the Hungarian Chamber of Auditors (MKVK) which governs bank auditors.

Market-infrastructure and capital-market bodies with governance publications were not covered: GIRO Zrt., KELER/KELER KSZF, Budapesti Értéktőzsde (BÉT), Országos Betétbiztosítási Alap (OBA), Befektető-védelmi Alap (BEVA), Bankkártya Szövetség-type card bodies.

Association governance changes are legally filed with the Hungarian courts (civil-organisation register, birosag.hu / Országos Bírósági Hivatal civil szervezetek névjegyzéke), which would give authoritative dated officer changes. This registry route was not explored in this pass.

No URL in this slice has been verified as reachable; several (hblf.hu, bcch.com, makisz.hu, blockchainhungary.org) use legacy or query-string URL schemes with elevated rot risk, and amcham.hu/bbj.hu may be partly gated.
